question: When restoring items with the Veeam Explorer restore wizard for Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365, what happens to existing items if I don't tick "Restore only latest version"?
gold_facts: If Restore only latest version is not selected, backed-up versions are merged with the existing versions in production.
If Restore only latest version is selected, you choose Merge or Overwrite.

A.text:
The sources give conflicting answers depending on the version of the documentation:

- In some versions, if "Restore only latest version" is not selected, **all versions of items in the production environment will be replaced with the relevant data from the backup file** [1][3][5][6].
- In other versions, if the check box is not selected, **backed-up versions of items will be merged with the existing versions in the production environment** [2][4].

So the behavior is either a full replacement of all versions with backup data [1][3][5][6] or a merge of backup versions with existing versions [2][4], depending on which documentation version applies to your product build.

documents.title: Step 6. Specify Restore Options
documents.text:
Step 6. Specify Restore Options
Step 6\. Specify Restore Options

At this step of the wizard, select check boxes next to the restore options that you want to apply and click Restore.

You can select the following options:

* Changed items. Allows you to restore data that has been modified in your production environment.
* Missing items. Allows you to restore missing items.
* Restore only latest version. Allows you to restore only the latest version of items. If this check box is selected, you can select one of the following options:

* Overwrite. To overwrite data in the production environment.
* Merge. To merge an existing and a backup version of items.

If the Restore only latest version check box is not selected, all versions of items in the production environment will be replaced with the relevant data from the backup file.

* Restore shared access. Allows you to restore shared access.

* Send a notification by email to the users with permissions to the file. Select this check box if you want to notify users about items restore. Veeam Explorer for Microsoft OneDrive will notify users with whom items have been shared. You can select this check box only if the Restore shared access check box is selected.

| Note |
| --- |
| The Send a notification by email to the users with permissions to the file check box is only available when restoring data from backups created by Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 for Microsoft 365 organizations. |

![Step 6. Specify Restore Options](/media/6d3c9a3b-bab5-4223-9cb1-f2aee6428c42/5cccaf9de89db655.png "Specify Restore Options")

> **Figure:** Restore Wizard dialog showing the 'Restore options' step, with checkboxes for restoring changed and missing items, restoring only the latest version, overwriting files, restoring shared access, and sending email notifications. The 'Restore' button is highlighted.

Step 5\. Specify Restore Options
================================

At this step of the wizard, select check boxes next to the restore options that you want to apply and click Restore.


You can select the following options:

question: What permissions does the SQL login need when I add an Azure SQL Server account in Veeam Data Cloud, and can I use Entra ID authentication?
gold_facts: The db_owner database-level role is also required, but only for backup operations.
Microsoft Entra ID authentication is not supported.

A.text:
**Microsoft:** The retrieved documentation does not cover adding an Azure SQL Server account in Veeam Data Cloud, so no Microsoft-side answer can be given from these facts.

**Veeam Data Cloud:** Azure SQL Server Accounts does not support Microsoft Entra ID authentication [11]. The Azure SQL account used to authenticate against the staging server must have the sysadmin server-level role assigned; otherwise, only the source SQL Server can be used as a staging server or the backup operation will fail [12], and otherwise the backup operation will fail [13]. Separately, when Entra ID authentication is used with SQL Server, the Azure SQL Server must have an Entra ID administrator that grants access to the Veeam service account application [9], specifically the Veeam service account application ID configured as its Entra ID administrator [10], and authorizing Veeam Data Cloud access to the Azure tenant requires the Application Administrator role (or a more privileged role) in Entra ID [14].

sources.paraphrase: To enable Microsoft Entra ID authentication, the Azure SQL Server must have an Entra ID administrator that grants access to the Veeam service account application.

documents.title: Step 5. Specify Policy Processing Settings
documents.text:
[Step 5. Specify Policy Processing Settings › Step 5. Specify Policy Processing Settings]

Configuring Entra ID Administrator

To enable Microsoft Entra ID authentication, the Azure SQL Server must have an Entra ID administrator that grants access to the [Veeam service account](azure_settings_accounts_service_view.html) application. You can do this in one of the following ways:

* Assign the Veeam service account application directly as the Entra ID administrator of the SQL Server.
* Add the Veeam service account application to a Microsoft Entra ID group, and assign that group as the Entra ID administrator of the SQL Server. Use this option if the SQL Server already has an administrator that you want to keep.


| Important |
| --- |
| The Entra ID administrator must be assigned through the Azure portal, as described in [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/authentication-aad-configure?view=azuresql&tabs=azure-portal). Any other assignment method is not supported and will cause backup operations to fail. |

sources.paraphrase: Azure SQL Server must have the Veeam service account application ID configured as its Entra ID administrator to enable Microsoft Entra ID authentication.

documents.title: Step 4. Specify Restore Settings
documents.text:
[Step 4. Specify Restore Settings › Step 4. Specify Restore Settings]


* Entra ID Application — select this option to use an Entra ID application.

To enable Microsoft Entra ID authentication, the Azure SQL Server must have the [Veeam service account](azure_settings_accounts_service_view.html) application ID configured as its Entra ID administrator. You can set the Entra ID administrator in the settings of the Azure SQL Server in the Azure portal. To learn more, see [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/authentication-aad-configure?view=azuresql&tabs=azure-portal).


* Username and Password — select this option to use an Azuse SQL account. In the SQL Account section, click Select account and choose the necessary SQL account.


Specifying SQL Server Settings

To specify settings for the target SQL Server that will host the restored database, do the following:

1. In the Server Settings section, from the Region list, select the region of the target SQL server.
2. From the SQL Server list, select the target SQL server that will host the restored database.
3. From the Elastic Pool drop\-down list, select an elastic pool to which the restored database will be added.

documents.title: Adding SQL Server Account
documents.text:
[Adding SQL Server Account › Adding SQL Server Account]
Adding SQL Server Account
=========================

To add a new SQL Server account, do the following:


1. In the Management section of the main menu, select Settings.
2. Select the Azure SQL Server Accounts tab and click Create.
3. In the Name field, enter a name for the account.


The maximum length of the account name is 32 characters. The following characters are supported: Latin letters, numeric characters, underscores and dashes. The following characters are not supported: \\ / " ' \[ ] : \| \< \> \+ \= ; , ? \* @ \& $.


1. In the Description field, enter a description of the account for future reference.
2. In the Username field, enter a user account that will be used to connect to SQL server.
3. In the Password field, enter the password for the user account that will be used to connect to SQL server.


| Important |
| --- |

| When you add a new database account, consider the following:* The specified credentials must belong to a user account that has the following roles assigned: The \#\#MS\_DatabaseManager\#\#, \#\#MS\_LoginManager\#\#, \#\#MS\_DatabaseConnector\#\# and \#\#MS\_DefinitionReader\#\# server\-level roles, and the db\_owner database\-level role. Consider that the db\_owner database\-level role is required for backup operations only.
 For more information on [server\-level roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/security/authentication-access/server-level-roles?view=sql-server-ver16) and [database\-level roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/security/authentication-access/database-level-roles?view=sql-server-ver16), see Microsoft Docs.
 * Microsoft Entra ID authentication is not supported. |

[

![Add Database Account](/media/71579a6a-4015-4fbb-8403-
d81de05a34e0/ebedc81e3a5a.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'New SQL server account' dialog in the Azure SQL Server Accounts settings, showing fields for Name, Description, Username, and Password, with the 'Create' button highlighted.

](images/azure_settings_accounts_database_add.png "Add Database Account")

documents.title: Step 2. Select Restore Point and Properties
documents.text:
[Step 2. Select Restore Point and Properties › Step 2. Select Restore Point and Properties]
Step 2\. Select Restore Point and Properties
============================================


At the Compare step of the wizard, select a restore point and properties that you want to restore. You can compare the property values in the selected restore point with the values in production or in another restore point.

To select a restore point and properties, do to following:


1. Choose the restore point from which you want to restore the data:

* To find a restore point in the restore point calendar, click the Restore point field.
* To change the restore point, click the Previous and Next links.
* To select the latest restore point, click Jump to latest.


1. By default, the list of properties shows only the properties that have changed. To show all properties, set the Show changes only toggle to Off.
2. In the list of properties, select the properties you want to restore.


In the Selected Restore Point Version and Comparison Version columns, you can see property values at different points in time. By default, the Comparison Version column displays the current values in production. To change them to the values from a specific restore point, click Production and select the restore point.

[

![Selecting Restore Point and Properties](/media/5f708075-b6c7-4752-abcd-6187bc4a3d57/79c5e4713e2b.png)


> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Compare & Restore Fields' dialog in Entra ID, showing the Compare step where a restore point (8/21/25, 9:06:09 AM) is selected. The table displays a change in 'Application Administrator' role assignment from false to true, marked as 'Added', with the 'Next' button highlighted for proceeding.

](images/entra_id_restore_prop_point.png "Selecting Restore Point and Properties")

Entra ID authentication is not supported for database accounts [3].
